verdicts.reason: Strongest of Y is its simple both-order gate; X keeps that but adds an ambition guard, a verifier family outside the final panel, and a no-reasons kill criterion, which answer Y's own listed failure modes.

Y's strength is a compact portfolio rule; X fits tau from saved residuals rather than fixing it at 0.5 SD, adds a minimum-comparison guard and a label-consistency fallback, and has explicit kill thresholds.

Y's strength is the claim ledger itself; X adds a witness-flip check against rigged scripts, a load-bearing flag, a 10-brief test with ambition and checkability kill criteria, which make it actually falsifiable.

Y's strength is the bounded repair loop with a template library; X adds claim re-extraction, a flag that ranks cards with struck load-bearing claims lower, and a matched-token prose-feedback control on 10 briefs with kill criteria.
Y's strength is boundary-focused effort concentration; X also re-ranks finals on fresh comparisons to avoid winner's-curse selection and adds a kill criterion on held-out child-beats-parent rate.

Y's strength is a residual head that reduces to BT with few labels; X additionally trains and scores on different-family panels and has an explicit bootstrap kill criterion, so Goodhart leakage is testable.
Y's strength is a principled judge-aware BT; X adds leave-one-brief-out evaluation, a crossed allocation factor, a per-judge cap and a kill criterion, making the claimed gain isolable.
Y's strength is a simple Thompson memory; X shrinks toward the global operator rate and pairs the primary test by brief, whereas Y's per-contest power calculation ignores within-brief correlation.

Y's strength is a simple one-verifier gate; X's placebo paraphrase directly measures the gate's style bias, adds two families and a no-reasons arm, and defines kill conditions relative to the placebo.

Y's strength is the posterior-max selection rule; X fits tau from data, caps the mean-of-3 loss, and degrades to plain top-3 when finalists are diverse, so it cannot cost much and has a clear kill rule.

Y's strength is the executable claim ledger; X adds codebase probes that make this brief's own feasibility claims checkable, a step-0 checkable-fraction measurement, and a neutral median score instead of ranking uncheckable cards last.

Y's strength is the check-repair loop with templates; X is standalone, token-capped, reverts cards left under 3 claims, and can be tested offline on saved finalists with kill criteria, so it is testable now.

Y's strength is the boundary-targeted mutation cycle; X adds a gate family separate from ranker and panel, a length-normalised view, and an overfit-gap measurement with kill thresholds, which address the main Goodhart risk.

Y's strength is a full residual selection head; X stages it so only sign-constrained nuisance penalties are free at first, uses within-run conditional logit and needs 5 briefs instead of 15, so it can be tested sooner with less overfitting risk.

Y's strength is a reliability-weighted BT; X adds shrinkage, a shared verbosity bias term and label-free bias calibration from probes, so part of it works without external labels and has a step-1 kill test.

Y's strength is similarity-weighted Thompson operator memory; X warm-starts offline from saved ideas, uses a non-mutator judge family with a length cap, and adds a cheap stage-1 chi-square test before the costly 30-brief run.
